This motivates optimizing the schedule to bring the generated action distribution closer to the demonstrations and improve task success. We propose Ground Your Steps (GYS), a training-free method that optimizes the sampling schedule by matching the generated and demonstrated chunk distributions at each observation. GYS applies truncated fractional differencing along each arm joint's action sequence and compares two types of pairwise differences between action chunks at each observation: differences of a generated chunk against a demonstration, and differences of two independent generated chunks against each other. After fractional differencing, these two pairwise-difference distributions coincide exactly when the distributions of generated and demonstrated action chunks match. GYS minimizes the energy distance between these distributions to obtain an improved schedule for each task and NFE budget. Compared with the uniform grid, GYS brings the generated chunk distribution closer to the demonstrated distribution and raises the success rate through the sampling schedule alone. On RoboTwin 2.0 benchmarks, GYS improves success rates at nearly every budget, with gains of 2.8 percentage points for both $π_{0.5}$ and GR00T N1.7. The gains also transfer to three real-world manipulation tasks, reaching up to 3.3 percentage points. Code is available at https://github.com/D-Robotics-AI-Lab/GroundYourSteps.
papers.title_zh: Ground Your Steps：优化流匹配机器人策略的采样调度
papers.summary_zh: 免训练地优化流匹配策略的采样步长调度，RoboTwin 2.0 上 π0.5 与 GR00T N1.7 均提升 2.8 个百分点。

papers.title: WAtcher: Watching Ahead for Safe Robotic Manipulation with Efficient World-Action Models
papers.comment: 12 pages, 4 figures, 6 tables. Project page: https://zyshan0929.github.io/WAtcher
papers.abstract: World-action models (WAMs) couple future imagination with action generation, but they execute every action chunk while ignoring the potential risk. To fill this gap, we present WAtcher, a safety-aware world-action framework in which the policy imagines the outcome of the candidate chunk before execution. For fast future preview, WAtcher builds on a compact WAM whose video expert imagines the visual outcome in only two denoising steps. In addition, we propose Safe-Guard, a lightweight module kept outside the WAM that scores each candidate chunk from its imagined outcome and triggers a bounded retreat when the risk is high. Safe-Guard is detachable and can be applied to other WAMs. To train Safe-Guard, we build an autonomous pipeline to collect hazard data from RoboTwin, LIBERO, and a real robot. Specifically, the pipeline perturbs expert demonstrations and labels each candidate chunk from the physical events recorded when it is executed, such as contacts and losses of support. Using the ~25,000 labeled windows from this pipeline, Safe-Guard reaches 92.1% balanced accuracy on a blind set, and cuts hazardous closed-loop trials on training tasks from 27.0% to 10.8% without lowering task success. On a held-out 300-question benchmark, it scores 94.2%, against 72.5% and 63.3% for zero-shot GPT-6-Astra and Claude Opus 5.5. WAtcher also reaches 90.4% and 82.4% average success on RoboTwin 2.0 and ManiSkill3, on par with or above leading WAMs, and 74.0% on five real-world tasks with Safe-Guard on, against 59.5% for $π_{0.5}$. Project page: https://zyshan0929.github.io/WAtcher
papers.title_zh: WAtcher：为安全机器人操作提前预览的高效世界-动作模型
papers.summary_zh: 在世界-动作模型上加可拆卸的 Safe-Guard，依据想象结果评分，训练任务上危险试验从 27.0% 降到 10.8%。

papers.title: CoTacWAM: Joint Modeling of Vision and Touch for Robotic Manipulation
papers.abstract: We present CoTacWAM, a world-action model that learns shared contact semantics between wrist vision and touch, achieving the best observed performance in our nominal manipulation and missing-input evaluations. The two modalities observe the same local interaction through different signals: wrist images reveal nearby geometry, while touch records physical contact. Our approach connects their common contact meaning while preserving the evidence unique to each modality, giving the policy a joint description of interaction across available input combinations. This representation supports predictive action learning alongside head-view scene context and conditions corrections after an independent detector confirms a failed attempt. Experiments across four real-world tasks demonstrate improved manipulation performance over the evaluated baselines, robustness to missing local observations, and further gains from autonomous retries.
papers.title_zh: CoTacWAM：机器人操作中视觉与触觉的联合建模
papers.summary_zh: 世界-动作模型学习腕部视觉与触觉共享的接触语义，四个真机任务上优于基线并支持自主重试。

papers.title: xFORM: Accelerating Fixed-Lag LiDAR Odometry with Exact Factor Compression
papers.abstract: Light Detection and Ranging (LiDAR) sensors are increasingly popular for state estimation because of their precision, long range, and high measurement rate. Unfortunately, LiDAR Odometry (LO) systems incur substantial computational cost when processing large point clouds, particularly those that jointly refine a window of scan poses. While our prior LO work FORM is real-time, the costs of feature extraction, correspondence search, and the evaluation and linearization of residuals during pose optimization can introduce significant latency. This latency makes downstream tasks such as control and path planning difficult. To overcome this, we present xFORM, which accelerates the three stages of FORM. xFORM uses factor compression to reduce an optimization problem involving hundreds of thousands of feature matches to 34 scalar residuals per scan pair, while preserving the original objective and Gauss-Newton system in exact arithmetic. We integrate this optimizer into two variants: xFORM-CPU, which additionally parallelizes feature extraction on the CPU, and xFORM-GPU, which accelerates feature processing, correspondence search, and factor compression on the GPU. Across fifteen complete sequences from three datasets, xFORM-CPU and xFORM-GPU achieve overall speedups of 1.1-1.4$\times$ and 2.0-4.0$\times$ over FORM, respectively, with no numerically significant differences to the original implementation.
papers.title_zh: xFORM：用精确因子压缩加速定滞后激光雷达里程计
papers.summary_zh: 把数十万特征匹配压缩为每对扫描 34 个标量残差，GPU 版比 FORM 快 2.0-4.0 倍且结果一致。

papers.title: WISER-RL: A Wake-Sleep Learning Mechanism for Robot Reinforcement Learning from One Demonstration
papers.abstract: A robot learning from one human demonstration may rarely succeed on its own, leaving reinforcement learning (RL) with little reward feedback. We introduce WISER-RL ({W}ake--sleep policy improvement loop, {I}mitation, and {S}elective {E}xperience {R}eplay), a composite reinforcement learning framework that turns assisted practice into autonomous control. During wake, GPTDAgger monitors disagreement among actions sampled by a diffusion policy. When disagreement crosses a threshold, a frozen GPT controller uses retrieved experience to continue the episode. During sleep, Conflict-Aware Experience Reweighting (CAER) compares visually matched successful trajectories and downweights conflicting action windows with more steps remaining to success. The policy imitates the reweighted successes and learns from both successes and failures through offline advantage-guided RL before collecting the next round. After final online PPO refinement, the autonomous policy succeeded in 100% evaluations on each of six LIBERO tasks and 100% trials on each of two real-robot tasks.
papers.title_zh: WISER-RL：基于单次演示的机器人强化学习的醒-睡学习机制
papers.summary_zh: 醒阶段用 GPT 控制器辅助探索，睡阶段重加权成功轨迹做离线优势引导 RL，LIBERO 六个任务和两个真机任务均达 100%。

papers.title: Ask to Land: Learning a Mask-Conditioned Open-Vocabulary Landing Policy via Differentiable Physics
papers.abstract: Existing drone landing systems, whether model-based or learning-based, typically rely on predefined visual markers (e.g., ArUco tags) or are trained for specific platform categories, and often assume structured target motion. Recent open-vocabulary studies enable text-prompted target selection, but integrating this capability with learned closed-loop landing control remains underexplored. To this end, we present \textit{Ask to Land}, a mask-conditioned framework that enables a quadrotor to land on various platforms described by a user in natural language, including randomly moving platforms. The core of our approach is the integration of a frozen state-of-the-art open-vocabulary perception frontend (YOLO-World with MobileSAM) and a control policy learned by differentiable physics. By providing real-time, task-agnostic semantic segmentation masks as policy inputs, our framework enables the drone to land on prompt-selected targets without target-specific fine-tuning while continuously tracking dynamic target motion during descent. The frozen frontend processes the prompt, while the policy receives the mask without text embeddings or category labels. To efficiently optimize the control policy, we leverage differentiable physics learning via Backpropagation-Through-Time (BPTT), and employ a carefully designed reward that enforces visual alignment with the landing target and altitude-adaptive descent speed, together with stable control. Real-world deployments validate that our approach achieves landings on diverse user-specified objects, including static and moving platforms.
papers.title_zh: Ask to Land：通过可微物理学习掩码条件的开放词汇降落策略
papers.summary_zh: 冻结开放词汇分割前端，用可微物理训练控制策略，使四旋翼降落到语言指定的静止或移动平台。

papers.title: X-World: Transferring Video Priors to Cross-Embodiment Robot Control
papers.abstract: Language-instructed manipulation requires robust closedloop policies, yet action-labeled robot trajectories are costly and limited in coverage. Human and robot videos provide complementary spatiotemporal priors for crossembodiment control. We propose X-World, which adapts pretrained video diffusion to variable views. A Q-Former compresses hidden states into tokens for a shared flowmatching expert that predicts action chunks. Datasetspecific projections map native states and actions. We adapt the backbone on large-scale robot and human videos, freeze it for action-only pretraining of the Q-Former and action expert, then post-train on the target platform. At inference, X-World responds at 20 Hz and overlaps updates with execution via asynchronous real-time chunking. X-World performs strongly on LIBERO and under zero-shot shifts on LIBERO-Plus. On hardware, it averages 81.7% success across six bimanual tasks on the side-mounted dual-arm UR5e, one of three real-robot configurations presented.
papers.title_zh: X-World：将视频先验迁移到跨本体机器人控制
papers.summary_zh: 把预训练视频扩散模型适配到多视角并接流匹配动作专家，双臂 UR5e 上六个任务平均成功率 81.7%。

papers.title: CoTAMP: Cooperative Task and Motion Planning for Quadruped Robots with Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Some environments cannot be traversed by a single quadruped robot, for example a ledge that one robot can climb only from its partner's back or a gap that must be bridged with boxes. Solving them requires cooperative task and motion planning (TAMP). Previous works are limited to the motions of a single robot or only select actions from a predefined set of skills. We propose a framework with two parts: task planning that invents motions not defined in advance, and motion generation that realizes the invented motions. Both parts consist of large language model (LLM)-based modules and code-based modules. Task planning divides the trajectory of the whole task into steps and fixes the robot poses at the step boundaries. Motion generation produces keyframes that describe the motion of each step and turns them into a continuous trajectory through kinematic synthesis. The code-based modules check every plan and motion and return failures to the LLM-based modules for correction. The whole trajectory is then refined by trajectory optimization to satisfy the dynamics. On three simulated courses with two RAIBO2 robot models, our framework produced kinematically valid references in all 30 trials, all of which converged in trajectory optimization. Compared with several baselines, our framework showed advantages in success rate, dynamic feasibility, execution time, and generation time and cost. Project page: https://woojin8098.github.io/CoTAMP/
papers.title_zh: CoTAMP：基于大语言模型的四足机器人协作任务与运动规划
papers.summary_zh: LLM 与代码模块协作生成并校验多四足机器人协作运动，三个仿真场景 30 次试验全部得到运动学有效参考。

papers.title: Integration of Vision-Language-Action Control for Autonomous Forklift Unloading with Limited Real-World Data
papers.abstract: Forklifts play a critical role in warehousing and distribution, but existing automation systems remain limited in handling complex tasks that require sequential decision-making. Recently, vision--language--action (VLA) models have emerged as a promising approach for multi-step decision-making by directly generating control actions from visual observations and language prompts. Although VLA-based control has been extensively researched for manipulators, to the best of our knowledge, its application to forklifts remains unexplored. Therefore, this study demonstrates the integration of VLA control for an autonomous forklift unloading task with limited real-world data. Moreover, training VLA models typically requires large-scale datasets. As there is currently no public dataset for forklift operations, we use a VLA model pretrained primarily on robotic manipulator data and construct a training dataset via simulation, which can be scaled up at low cost. We then adapt the pretrained VLA model to forklift control using 9.38 h of simulation data and 0.8 h of real-world demonstrations, with the latter accounting for approximately 8% of the collected forklift data by duration. The integrated system was validated through 72 real-world trials across four model variants. The results show that the proposed system can accomplish an unloading task even with limited real-world data.
papers.title_zh: 在有限真实数据下集成 VLA 控制用于自主叉车卸货
papers.summary_zh: 用 9.38 小时仿真数据加 0.8 小时真实演示微调预训练 VLA，72 次真机试验完成叉车卸货。

papers.title: SentryWard: Formal Verification of Warp-Specialized GPU Kernels
papers.abstract: Modern GPU kernels overlap asynchronous data movement, computation on general-purpose cores (e.g., CUDA cores), and computation on specialized cores (e.g., tensor cores) using warp specialization. These asynchronous-overlap optimizations introduce complex synchronization requirements, where incorrect ordering of asynchronous operations can lead to data races, premature resource reuse, and incorrect results. Testing alone cannot guarantee correctness because such errors are nondeterministic and may only manifest in rare execution schedules, and existing GPU formal verification techniques have limited support for warp-specialized kernels. We present SentryWard, a framework for formally verifying warp-specialized GPU kernels. SentryWard integrates synchronization verification, data-race and resource-lifetime analysis, and functional equivalence checking. The key idea is to establish that synchronization induces the same ordering constraints across all possible execution schedules. SentryWard extends this well-synchronization analysis to modern GPU barriers with asynchronous transaction tracking and derives a schedule-independent happens-before graph. It then uses this graph to verify memory safety and construct symbolic output expressions for functional equivalence checking. While SentryWard generally assumes tensor shapes and kernel launch configurations are given and unrolls loops, it uses compact representations of repeated structures across threads and tensor computations to improve scalability. SentryWard is publicly available at https://github.com/gpu-verifier/sentryward.
papers.title_zh: SentryWard：warp 特化 GPU kernel 的形式化验证
papers.summary_zh: 通过与调度无关的 happens-before 图验证 warp 特化 kernel 的同步、数据竞争与功能等价，已开源。

papers.title: $\widetilde{\varepsilon}$: Does Initial Noise Induce Directional Bias in Vision-Language-Action Models?
papers.abstract: Vision-language-action models (VLAs) have widely adopted diffusion-based action generation for continuous robot motions, enabling fine-grained control across diverse tasks. However, recent studies have shown that their performance is highly sensitive to initial noise, with resulting action errors that make recovery difficult during execution. Existing approaches search for favorable noise initializations to improve performance, yet the action expert itself remains sensitive to noise. In this work, we reveal that initial noise induces a consistent directional bias in action space that closely aligns with the noise's temporal mean. We thus introduce a simple yet effective framework that improves robustness to initial noise through interventions during both training and inference. During training, we enforce consistent action predictions from antithetic noise pairs $(ε, -ε)$ and, at inference, remove the noise's temporal mean. Our method substantially reduces action deviation and improves task performance across simulation benchmarks. In real-robot experiments, our method increases the average task success rate of $π_{0.5}$ from 40% to 68%, with more stable and consistent execution.
papers.title_zh: ε̃：初始噪声会在视觉-语言-动作模型中引入方向性偏差吗？
papers.summary_zh: 发现初始噪声造成与其时间均值对齐的动作偏差，用对偶噪声一致性训练并去均值，真机上 π0.5 成功率从 40% 升到 68%。

papers.title: Explicit covers and rigid obstructions for simplicial complexity: from spheres to surfaces
papers.comment: 22 pages, 6 tables, 1 algorithm. Code: https://github.com/MiguelPerezI/chain-first-annealer ; certificates: https://github.com/MiguelPerezI/simplicial-complexity-certificates (tag arxiv-v1)
papers.abstract: The strict simplicial complexity $SC_{\rm strict}(K)$, González's simplicial complexity at subdivision level zero, is one less than the least number of contiguity domains covering the ordered product $K\times K$. We bound it from both sides. For upper bounds, every product of two vertex stars is a domain, which gives $SC_{\rm strict}(K)\leρ(K)-1$ for an exactly computable set-cover number $ρ(K)$; the bound is sharp on every even-dimensional simplex boundary. A GPU annealer that evolves whole systems of contiguity chains finds three-domain covers of $\partialΔ^3,\dots,\partialΔ^7$ and of the cube boundary. Seeded by star covers, it descends from $24$ to $5$ domains on the icosahedron boundary, and an exact SAT completion of its stalled state gives $SC_{\rm strict}\le3$ there. For lower bounds, a subcomplex of $K\times K$ is rigid if its two projections are joined by no contiguity chain of any length; $k$ domains can cover $K\times K$ only if $k$ classes of facets avoid every rigid subcomplex, a finite SAT problem. Rigid subcomplexes arise from hollow triangles over essential empty triangles and, on complexes without dominated vertices, from the graph of every order-preserving simplicial self-map other than the identity. The resultingchain-length-free bounds give $SC_{\rm strict}(\partialΔ^{n+1})=2>1=TC(S^n)$ for $n=3,5,7,9$, $SC_{\rm strict}=2>1$ for the five-vertex Möbius band, $SC_{\rm strict}\ge3>2$ for the seven-vertex torus, and $4\le SC_{\rm strict}\le5$ and $4\le SC_{\rm strict}\le6$ for two triangulations of $\mathbb{RP}^2$. They also sort the annealer's stalls: on these two triangulations of $\mathbb{RP}^2$, the Klein bottle and $\partialΔ^4$, almost every uncovered facet closes a rigid subcomplex in every domain, while the icosahedron stall was a search failure.
papers.title_zh: 单纯复形复杂度的显式覆盖与刚性障碍：从球面到曲面
papers.summary_zh: 从上下两侧给出严格单纯复形复杂度的界，并给出球面与曲面的显式覆盖和可验证证书。

papers.title: FailPoint-X: A Policy-Matched, Failure-Anchored Benchmark for Offline VLA Post-Training from Human Takeovers
papers.comment: 34 pages (8-page main paper, references, and 24-page supplementary material), 9 figures, 20 tables. Zirui Li and Yujie Yan contributed equally. Project page: https://lzrbit.github.io/FailPoint_X/ ; Code: https://github.com/yujieyan81/failpoint-x
papers.abstract: Human takeovers offer corrective supervision for vision-language-action (VLA) policies, but their contribution to offline post-training must be separated from that of continued optimization. We introduce FailPoint-X, a benchmark for offline VLA post-training with human takeovers. To represent uncertainty in failure onset, an annotator marks an interval for each failure, and training takeovers start at seeded frames sampled within it. From one fixed $π_{0.5}$ checkpoint, which also initializes post-training, we assemble 629 natural failures across 10 LIBERO-X task families at up to five difficulty levels. All 2,823 takeover attempts are logged; 2,400 are accepted recoveries, of which 2,320 are used for post-training. Evaluation restarts every method from the fixed midpoints of 384 held-out failure intervals. Under matched actor-update counts, we compare behavior cloning of recoveries, value-based offline learning on recoveries and failed rollouts, and continued training on existing demonstrations. Within 1,200 steps on the 240 L1-L3 held-out failures, cloning improves recovery by 29.4 percentage points (pp) over the demonstration-only control; the value-based learner does not establish a further gain (1.5 pp). In exploratory evaluation from L1-L5 nominal starts at the same horizon, cloning loses 30.0 pp of success relative to the base policy; mixing in demonstrations reduces the loss to 16.5 pp, a reduction that shrinks under a stricter, pre-specified horizon. Restorable failure states and a shared evaluator let all methods be compared from identical starts.
papers.title_zh: FailPoint-X：面向人类接管的离线 VLA 后训练的策略匹配、失败锚定基准
papers.summary_zh: 构建以人类接管为监督的离线 VLA 后训练基准，区分接管数据与持续优化各自的贡献。

papers.title: RegHarness: Regulating What Code-as-Policy Agents Keep from Steps to Skills
papers.abstract: Code-as-Policy agents generate, execute, and revise robot programs, but often lack explicit mechanisms to govern what persists across executions: which actions are retained within a trial and which code modifications carry over to subsequent runs. This leaves two critical aspects of agent behavior insufficiently controlled: step-level execution and cross-run adaptation. We present RegHarness, a two-level harness that governs both forms of persistence for the RATs agent team, without relying on a vision-language-action (VLA) policy or demonstrations. Within each trial, run-time governance evaluates each proposed step from a reset scene, replaying the committed steps, while a fixed-rule controller commits the step only when both RATs' verifier and a task-long LLM auditor approve it. Between runs, a coding agent uses logged failures to develop and test revisions to skills, primitives, and rules, which remain disabled by default until explicitly enabled by the authors. Using a single low-cost model across all run-time roles, RegHarness achieves an 87.8% success rate (158/180) on paired LIBERO-PRO trials, compared with 39.4% for RATs, and a 72.0% success rate on MolmoSpaces trials. A $2\times2$ ablation study of RegHarness's two levels shows that its skill refinement alone increases RATs' successful trials from 71 to 135, whereas run-time governance alone achieves 105 and RATs' native stepwise reset-and-replay mode achieves only 46. These findings suggest that, for Code-as-Policy agents operating with low-cost models, task success depends not only on how generated programs are executed, but also on the quality of the reusable skills they invoke and how those skills evolve across runs.
papers.title_zh: RegHarness：规范 Code-as-Policy 智能体从步骤到技能的保留内容
papers.summary_zh: 为 Code-as-Policy 机器人智能体设计机制，控制单次执行内保留哪些动作、跨执行保留哪些代码修改。

papers.title: PROVE: Predict-to-Specify and Observe-to-Verify for Human-Aligned Evaluation of Mobile Manipulation
papers.abstract: Judging open-world robot manipulation is hard because layouts, articulated fixtures, and valid goal configurations vary widely. On RoboCasa365, simulator predicates agree with human judgments on only 69.09\% of rollouts, and a frontier VLM judge on 86.12\%. We present \textbf{PROVE} (Predict-to-Specify, Observe-to-Verify), which first specifies what success should look like and then checks the outcome. PROVE refines success conditions from the instruction, the initial scene, a target-object reference image, and a generated goal image. The goal image only sharpens the conditions and never serves as evidence. On 6,500 human-annotated rollouts over 65 atomic actions, PROVE reaches \textbf{96.83\%} agreement. Applied to open-source policies, it reports far lower success than native checks and changes their ranking. To reduce evaluation overhead in policy learning, we distill PROVE into \textbf{PROVE-Lite}, a 4B evaluator that needs no reference images. In one forward pass, PROVE-Lite predicts the outcome and the terminal state of each task condition. It reaches \textbf{91.20\%} agreement while running about 38$\times$ faster than PROVE. Mapped to a severity-aware reward, its diagnoses improve PPO post-training over both simulator and binary rewards.
papers.title_zh: PROVE：面向移动操作人类对齐评测的“预测指定、观察验证”方法
papers.summary_zh: 先预测目标配置再观察验证，使移动操作评测与人类判断的一致率超过仿真谓词和 VLM 裁判。

papers.title: RoboJackVR: Turning Robot Tasks into VR Games for Scalable Demonstration Collection
papers.abstract: Scaling robot demonstration datasets requires collection systems that accommodate more participants and diverse tasks, yet teleoperation barriers and task-adaptation effort limit this expansion. We present RoboJackVR, a standalone virtual reality (VR) game in which players manipulate simulated robots to execute combat skills and contribute demonstrations. MuJoCo simulation and demonstration recording run locally on the headset, removing the need for an external PC or simulation server during collection. Tutorials, skill selection, combat consequences, and character progression organize repeated task attempts within a continuing game. Task contracts declare assets, controls, resets, success criteria, and recording semantics; separate game configurations specify guidance, attempt groups, skill effects, and course placement. Shared bindings connect these declarations to task execution, outcome handling, and recording, allowing tasks to reuse the game flow while retaining their control and success semantics. Batch tools package supported resources and generate configurations, with manual adaptation and review for new interfaces and unsupported predicates. We instantiate the approach with SO101-Nexus-derived and LIBERO tasks. On the 66 LIBERO-90 tasks covered by the collected data, ACT policies trained solely on VR demonstrations retain approximately 91% of the full-standard simulation-demonstration baseline's success rate on held-out initial states, averaged over four training seeds. These results support the utility of play-collected VR demonstrations for policy learning in this setting.
papers.title_zh: RoboJackVR：把机器人任务变成 VR 游戏以规模化采集示教
papers.summary_zh: 用独立 VR 游戏让玩家操控仿真机器人执行战斗技能，从而收集机器人示教数据。

papers.title: A general-purpose safe manipulator planning framework for diverse environments without retraining
papers.comment: 46 pages, 7 figures; main text and supplementary materials
papers.abstract: Nowadays, robots need to be retrained whenever their operating environment changes, and this prohibitive training cost keeps them far from daily use. The community is calling for innovations that bestow on a robot the ability to safely grasp different objects under different conditions without excessive training data and computing power. In response to this call, we present a general-purpose manipulator mission-planning framework, allowing a robot to safely perform manipulation tasks, such as grasping objects that fit in its gripper, across different operating environments without retraining its controllers. The framework rests on two innovations: a finite-state abstracted model, bisimilar to the original system dynamics, that describes accessibility of the space in front of the robot under its given arm and gripper, and a block-conservative specification generation method that turns each manipulation task under any specific operational environment into specifications about state accessibility of the abstracted model. A task proven feasible and safe on the abstracted model is guaranteed to be safe and achievable by the robot. Real-world case studies conducted on a Unitree G1 U1 humanoid show that manipulation tasks commonly encountered in daily life, such as grasping an object, pressing an elevator button or picking up a berry, can be handled within this framework, where an abstracted model of the G1 U1 robot is built only once to avoid costly model reconstructions, and different tasks are simply captured by specific block-conservative specifications, achievable by a generic mission planner with vision-based feedback control.
papers.title_zh: 无需重训即可适应多样环境的通用安全机械臂规划框架
papers.summary_zh: 提出无需针对新环境重训的机械臂安全抓取规划框架，面向不同物体与条件。

papers.title: $\mathrm{M}^{2}$-WAM: Efficient Hierarchical Memory Across Modalities and Timescales for World-Action Models
papers.abstract: Long-horizon robotic manipulation requires historical context, yet retaining extensive visual histories incurs growing storage and retrieval costs, while aggressive compression risks losing fine-grained information needed for subsequent decisions. Moreover, executed action histories capture intermediate behaviors that sparse visual observations may miss. Preserving this complementary context efficiently calls for modality-specific memory mechanisms that balance recent detail with long-term retention. To this end, we introduce $\mathrm{M}^{2}$-WAM, a world-action model equipped with hierarchical visual and interaction memories. $\mathrm{M}^{2}$-WAM preserves recent visual observations in dense short-term memory while consolidating entries evicted from this window into fixed-size associative long-term memory through gated delta updates. Within the same short- and long-term hierarchy, interaction memory encodes executed action prefixes into compact temporal representations, complementing visual observations with behavioral context. These complementary memories are integrated into world-action modeling through layer-wise retrieval, enabling memory-augmented action generation with a bounded online memory footprint independent of episode length. On the memory-dependent simulation benchmarks MIKASA-Robo and RMBench, $\mathrm{M}^{2}$-WAM achieves +53.2% and +61.2% absolute improvements in average success rates over Fast-WAM, respectively. These gains extend to real-world manipulation, where $\mathrm{M}^{2}$-WAM achieves a +29.3% absolute improvement over LingBot-VA in average success across three tasks. These results suggest that $\mathrm{M}^{2}$-WAM offers a promising approach to efficient memory-augmented world-action modeling.
papers.title_zh: M²-WAM：面向世界-动作模型的跨模态、跨时间尺度高效分层记忆
papers.summary_zh: 为世界-动作模型设计跨模态、跨时间尺度的分层记忆，降低长时程操作的历史存储与检索成本。

papers.title: Lab2Sim: Agentic Generation of Interactive Laboratory Equipment from Operation Videos
papers.abstract: Generating laboratory assets that faithfully reproduce the appearance, structure, and joint motions of real equipment remains challenging. Existing asset generation methods struggle to directly generate simulation assets for all equipment observed in operation videos and to faithfully reproduce the appearance, joint motions, and internal cavities of the real equipment. To address the challenge, we present Lab2Sim, an agentic framework that generates editable, simulation-ready laboratory equipment assets from egocentric or multi-view operation videos. Lab2Sim comprises four specialized agents. The Evidence Agent combines video observations with laboratory knowledge to specify equipment parts, materials, and functional requirements, which guide the Asset Agent in constructing editable Blender assets. The independent Verifier checks the generated geometry and appearance against the evidence and requirements, providing targeted feedback for revision. The Simulation Integration Agent converts verified Blender assets into simulation instances with physical properties and articulated mechanisms, using execution feedback to refine their behavior. Experiments on human and robot laboratory scenes show that Lab2Sim achieves higher visual fidelity and stronger interaction capability than coding-agent and real-to-sim baselines, including a Codex baseline using the same underlying model. We further demonstrate valve-controlled drainage and use the generated asset library to reproduce laboratory scenes and operations in RoboTwin, supporting reusable simulation environments for robotic laboratory tasks.
papers.title_zh: Lab2Sim：从操作视频智能体式生成可交互实验室设备
papers.summary_zh: 从操作视频出发，用智能体生成外观、结构和关节运动都忠实的实验室设备仿真资产。

papers.title: Systematic study of the performance of small robots on controlled laboratory substrates
papers.abstract: The design of robots able to locomote effectively over a diversity of terrain requires detailed ground interaction models; unfortunately such models are lacking due to the complicated response of real world substrates which can yield and flow in response to loading. To advance our understanding of the relevant modeling and design issues, we conduct a comparative study of the performance of DASH and RoACH, two small, biologically inspired, six legged, lightweight (10 cm, 20 g) robots fabricated using the smart composite microstructure (SCM) process. We systematically examine performance of both robots on rigid and flowing substrates. Varying both ground properties and limb stride frequency, we investigate average speed, mean mechanical power and cost of transport, and stability. We find that robot performance and stability is sensitive to the physics of ground interaction: on hard ground kinetic energy must be managed to prevent yaw, pitch, and roll instability to maintain high performance, while on sand the fluidizing interaction leads to increased cost of transport and lower running speeds. We also observe that the characteristic limb morphology and kinematics of each robot result in distinct differences in their abilities to traverse different terrains. Our systematic studies are the first step toward developing models of interaction of limbs with complex terrain as well as developing improved limb morphologies and control strategies.
papers.title_zh: 小型机器人在受控实验室基质上的性能系统研究
papers.summary_zh: 在受控颗粒基质上系统测试小型机器人的运动表现，为地面相互作用建模提供依据。

papers.title: FreshVLA: Frequency-Regularized Time Scale Hierarchical Latent Actions for Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.abstract: Learning reusable latent actions from action-free videos offers an effective route to improving Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies. However, reconstruction-oriented latent actions do not necessarily benefit policy learning: as they may encode task-irrelevant static appearance with scene identity, or entangle slowly varying task progress with fine-grained execution dynamics in limited discrete code. We propose FreshVLA, a VLA framework built on a frequency-guided, dynamics-sensitive learning paradigm for acquiring temporally hierarchical continuous latent actions. FreshVLA uses a high-pass prior to guide visual transition encoding toward dynamical regions, thereby reducing reliance on static appearance cues. It further organizes latent actions into coarse-grained task progress and fine-grained execution dynamics through cross-timescale sampling and frequency-domain regularization, enhancing their capacity to represent long-horizon behaviors. During policy training, we freeze the pretrained latent action encoder and transfer its representations to robot control through joint flow-matching of latent and robot actions. FreshVLA achieves 98.2% average success on LIBERO and 98.0% on LIBERO-Long, exceeding GR00T-N1.6 on the latter by 3.6%. It also reaches an average sequence length of 4.52 on CALVIN and strong overall success rate of 80.4% in the zero-shot LIBERO-PLUS evaluation. Furthermore, FreshVLA exhibits greater robustness to visual perturbations and a more distinct division of roles between two branches in modeling low- and high-frequency motion, respectively. In 35-step action regression, it achieves a 51.3-percentage-point higher relative error reduction than its hierarchical discrete counterpart. Real-world experiments demonstrate that FreshVLA improves the average success rate over $π_{0.5}$ by 7.5%. The FreshVLA project page is available at https://freshvla.github.io/.
papers.title_zh: FreshVLA：频率正则化的时间尺度分层潜在动作 VLA 模型
papers.summary_zh: 用频率正则化和时间尺度分层从无动作视频中学习潜在动作，改进 VLA 策略。

papers.title: DFLAT: Model-based Diffusion on Differentially Flat Spaces for Long-Horizon Trajectory Optimization
papers.abstract: Long-horizon diffusion-based planning for kinodynamically constrained systems requires both scalability and feasibility, yet existing diffusion planners typically sacrifice one for the other. We present DFLAT, a diffusion-based planning algorithm that operates directly on a differentially flat trajectory representation. Instead of diffusing over time-discretized controls, DFLAT denoises a compact set of Hermite curve parameters in the flat-output space, consisting of intermediate waypoints together with the endpoint tangents of each segment. Every denoised sample maps to a dynamically consistent trajectory, so feasibility holds by construction rather than being restored afterward. Experiments on challenging tractor-trailer planning benchmarks show that DFLAT matches or exceeds the success rates of existing baselines at consistently lower planning times, particularly on long-horizon problems requiring multiple forward-reverse maneuvers. In cases where kinodynamic RRT requires over 100 seconds, DFLAT plans in subsecond time, enabling practical deployment.
papers.title_zh: DFLAT：在微分平坦空间上做基于模型的扩散以优化长时程轨迹
papers.summary_zh: 在微分平坦轨迹表示上直接做扩散规划，兼顾长时程规划的可扩展性与可行性。

papers.title: Skeptic: Grounding Failure Diagnosis for Robot Skill Discovery
papers.abstract: Robot agents discover reusable skills by revising programs from execution feedback and retaining experience for later tasks. This process can fail when an agent treats an unsuccessful program as evidence that the task is physically impossible, ending exploration with revision budget remaining. We study this failure in Qwen3.8-27B and examine two decisions that shape skill discovery: I) how execution failures are diagnosed, and II) which lessons enter the shared skill library. Failure diagnosis requires the agent to reconstruct physical action effects from multimodal traces, while independent reproduction of a proposed repair does not require adequate task performance from its source program. We introduce Skeptic, a training-free protocol that uses measured action outcomes to guide repair and measured task success to govern skill admission. A grounded event log reports action effects and object end states from depth images and proprioception, separating sensor observations from inferred diagnoses. Verified promotion adds a development-success requirement on the source program to the existing independent reproduction check. Across 60 audited tasks, the mean number of tasks with false impossibility judgments decreases from 19.5 to 8.5 per campaign. On 80 LIBERO-Pro tasks and seven Robosuite tasks, Skeptic improves held-out success by 14.9 and 11.7 percentage points, with frozen model weights and the same program-revision budget.
papers.title_zh: Skeptic：面向机器人技能发现的落地式失败诊断
papers.summary_zh: 诊断机器人技能发现中把失败程序误判为任务物理上不可行的问题，并比较两种应对方式。

papers.title: Cross-Layer Characterization and AI-Assisted Diagnosis of C-to-Rust Performance
papers.abstract: Migrating C code to Rust can significantly improve software security, but understanding the performance implications of such migrations remains challenging. While Rust is often claimed to match C's performance, runtime safety checks, compiler optimizations, and hardware microarchitecture interact in ways that complicate performance diagnosis. We first conduct a systematic cross-layer characterization of 12 benchmarks comprising C implementations and their Rust counterparts. Our study reveals that runtime safety checks do not necessarily dominate performance overhead, as compiler and microarchitectural optimizations often mitigate their costs. Across 8 of the 12 benchmarks, at least one Rust implementation performs within 10% of its C counterpart or outperforms it. Motivated by these findings, we introduce FerroScope, an AI-assisted performance debugger that integrates source-level analysis, compiler optimization remarks, dynamic instruction traces, and hardware performance counters to diagnose performance differences between C and Rust. FerroScope reproduces our manual findings while providing more precise explanations in several cases, including identifying compiler optimizations inhibited by redundant bounds checks. Guided by these diagnoses, we develop an LLVM compiler pass that hoists redundant bounds checks through guarded loop versioning while preserving Rust's panic behavior. The pass enables downstream compiler optimizations, including loop unrolling and conditional-move conversion, reducing Selection Sort's overhead from 2.95x to 1.00x and improving Merge Sort from 1.43x to 0.91x relative to C. Together, our results demonstrate how cross-layer performance characterization and AI-assisted diagnosis can guide safety-preserving compiler optimizations for efficient C-to-Rust migration.
papers.title_zh: C 到 Rust 迁移性能的跨层刻画与 AI 辅助诊断
papers.summary_zh: 跨运行时检查、编译器优化和微架构多个层面，刻画并诊断 C 迁移到 Rust 后的性能差异。

papers.title: FOCI: Trajectory Optimization on Gaussian Splats for Gaussian Robots
papers.abstract: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) has recently gained popularity as a faster alternative to Neural Radiance Fields (NeRFs) in 3D reconstruction and view synthesis methods. Leveraging the spatial information encoded in 3DGS, this work proposes FOCI (Field Overlap Collision Integral), an algorithm that is able to optimize trajectories directly on the Gaussians themselves. FOCI leverages a novel and interpretable collision formulation for 3DGS using the notion of the overlap integral between Gaussians. The formulation presented applies to different robot morphologies (e.g., fixed and mobile base manipulators, legged robots, UAVs) and handles both static and dynamic Gaussian-Splat environments. Contrary to other approaches, which represent the robot with conservative bounding boxes that underestimate the traversability of the environment, we propose to represent the environment and the robot as Gaussian Splats. This not only has desirable computational properties, but also allows for orientation-aware planning, allowing the robot to pass through very tight and narrow spaces. We extensively test our algorithm in both synthetic and real Gaussian Splats, showcasing that collision-free trajectories for legged, aerial and manipulator robots can be computed in seconds, even with hundreds of thousands of Gaussians making up the environment. The code is available at https://github.com/leggedrobotics/foci
papers.title_zh: FOCI：在高斯点云上为高斯机器人做轨迹优化
papers.summary_zh: 提出场重叠碰撞积分算法，直接在 3DGS 表示上优化机器人轨迹。

papers.title: Why Does Sensor Depth Fail Learned Manipulation Policies? Finding the Failure Mode with ACT
papers.abstract: Learned manipulation policies, from task-specific imitation policies to vision-language-action (VLA) models, rely primarily on RGB images. While some studies report gains from sensor depth, others avoid depth cameras because of measurement noise. Depth cameras introduce both noise and missing depth values (holes), whose relative effects remain unclear. In this study, we calibrate a sensor model using a real wrist-mounted stereo camera and separately evaluate noise and holes on RGB-D imitation policies with three visual encoders in simulation. We found that complete depth improves success by approximately ten percentage points, and most of this gain persists even at twenty times the camera's noise level. In contrast, holes covering about one-sixth of the wrist image eliminate the detectable benefit of depth. The validity mask strongly influences depth reliance: marking a small fraction of pixels as invalid reduces reliance, while filling holes and marking them valid restores most of the benefit. Policies trained on clean depth also lose performance when holes appear only at deployment, sometimes falling below RGB-only performance. These findings suggest that depth cameras for learned policies should therefore be judged by depth coverage more than measurement precision.
papers.title_zh: 为何传感器深度会让学习型操作策略失效？用 ACT 找出失效模式
papers.summary_zh: 用 ACT 区分深度相机噪声与缺失值（空洞）各自对学习型操作策略的影响。

papers.title: 3AGameFactory-Motion: Agentic Rigging and Reliable Complex Motion Generation for Diverse 3D Assets
papers.abstract: Animating arbitrary 3D assets from instructions requires both structural inference and motion control, yet existing motion benchmarks mostly cover conventional human or animal skeletons with simple instructions. We introduce DivDynBench, which evaluates rigging and motion generation across six morphology categories, with instructions requiring multi-phase part coordination and explicit timing, angle, repetition, and trajectory constraints. With large language models, we systematically compare three common paradigms: specialized motion generation, video generation followed by motion recovery, and direct agent-driven generation. We analyze their control capabilities, cross-morphology adaptability, and generation costs. Guided by this comparison, we propose an Agentic Motion Framework in which an agent writes compact parametric skeleton and motion programs, and a deterministic executor performs rigging, kinematic solving, and geometric correction. Compact parameter control reduces generation overhead and improves rigging reliability and motion-control accuracy, providing practical guidance for deploying complex 3D motion generation.
papers.title_zh: 3AGameFactory-Motion：面向多样 3D 资产的智能体式绑定与可靠复杂动作生成
papers.summary_zh: 提出覆盖六类形态的绑定与动作生成基准 DivDynBench，并用智能体流程为任意 3D 资产生成动作。

papers.title: Embo-Harness: Towards Understanding Frontier-Model-as-Policy Harness
papers.abstract: Frontier multimodal models exhibit extraordinary generalization in generating robot actions from observations and instructions, enabling a new paradigm in which they serve directly as policies within closed-loop robotic harnesses. However, the design principles of such harnesses, and the capabilities underlying their strong performance, remain unclear. We present Embo-Harness, a framework for systematically studying frontier-model-as-policy harnesses. We investigate four components of the robotic agentic loop, namely, prompting, planning, action execution, and tool use, and distill six empirical findings into a practical recipe. This recipe prioritizes interfaces that exploit the model's native visual reasoning and tool-use capabilities over handcrafted plans, skills, or action priors, and identifies effective choices for action representation, chunking, reasoning effort, visual observations, short multi-action sequences, and policy refinement. On RoboLab-120, Embo-Harness achieves an 83.3\% success rate, outperforming the strongest reported baseline by 26.2 percentage points. It also succeeds in 15 of 20 zero-shot trials across four real-world manipulation tasks. Beyond performance, controlled interventions indicate that the studied model depends more strongly on accurate spatial target estimation than on explicit low-level joint or trajectory generation. These results provide both a practical recipe for building strong frontier-model-as-policy harnesses and a clearer account of the capabilities that drive their performance.
papers.title_zh: Embo-Harness：理解以前沿模型为策略的 Harness
papers.summary_zh: 研究把前沿多模态模型直接当作机器人策略的闭环 Harness，分析其设计原则与能力来源。

papers.title: RUIBench: What Makes a Good Robot-Use Interface?
papers.abstract: Foundation models can reason about complex physical tasks, yet translating this intelligence into reliable robot execution remains challenging. We argue that a critical, often overlooked factor is the robot-use interface (RUI), which determines how agents express and execute physical actions. To systematically study its impact, we introduce RUIBench, comprising 30 manipulation tasks across five suites spanning world knowledge, in-context learning, discovery, dynamic interaction, and contact-rich manipulation. We further develop RUIKit, a unified framework that crosses six action abstractions with two interaction forms, yielding 13 interfaces under shared perception and control. In simulation, changing only the RUI shifts a frontier agent's success rate from 45% to 81%, and that of a fine-tuned 4B model from 13% to 47%. Our analysis reveals that effective interfaces reduce unnecessary decisions while preserving essential feedback, with their benefits shaped by agent behavior and physical uncertainty. We further uncover a verification gap, where agents frequently declare success despite observable failures, revealing the need for task-level verification beyond individual actions. Together, these findings establish RUI design as a critical factor in embodied agent reliability.
papers.title_zh: RUIBench：什么样的机器人使用接口才是好接口？
papers.summary_zh: 提出 RUIBench，系统比较智能体表达和执行物理动作的接口对机器人任务表现的影响。

papers.title: From Rewarding What Models Say to How They Think: Attention Process Reward Model for LLM Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) has become an important component in large language models (LLMs). However, existing RL approaches focus on final outputs or textual solution trajectories, leading to coarse-grained rewards and unreliable reasoning. Such paradigms focus mainly on what the model outputs while overlooking how the model internally reasons. Therefore, can we reward how a model thinks internally rather than merely what it says? We first reveal the problem of textual reward aliasing in existing reward modeling approaches. Motivated by this, we propose the Attention Process Reward Model (APRM), which assigns internal rewards based on hidden states and attention maps to capture high-quality reasoning patterns. With only approximately 46M parameters, APRM is trained using ranking and counterfactual objectives, and its reward guides RL optimization while being periodically updated to handle distribution shifts. Integrated with representative RL methods, APRM achieved an average pass@8 gain of 2.88\%. Our results demonstrate the promise of incorporating internal reasoning signals into RL for LLMs.
papers.title_zh: 从奖励模型说了什么到它如何思考：面向 LLM 强化学习的注意力过程奖励模型
papers.summary_zh: 利用模型内部注意力构造过程奖励，让 LLM 强化学习奖励其推理过程而非只看输出。

papers.title: World Models as Native Latent Action Models
papers.comment: 19 pages, 7 figures, 6 tables. Project page: https://pawteam-eai.github.io/native-lam/
papers.abstract: Large and diverse video sources, such as egocentric human video and heterogeneous robot recordings, carry rich dynamics but come either without actions or without a shared action space. Latent action models (LAMs) can recover these dynamics, but they train their inverse- and forward-dynamics models (IDM, FDM) from scratch, trading off pixel reconstruction against latent capacity and accuracy. Pretrained video world models natively generate high-fidelity dynamics, yet represent them densely, entangled across all layers. Viewing the world model as a LAM, we show that these dynamics can be extracted with minimal changes to the model. Native LAM operates one pretrained video diffusion transformer as both IDM and FDM, with learnable dynamics registers as the only causal bridge between the two, and trains on counterfactual temporal pairs that differ in motion alone, so that the registers distill a video's dynamics into a compact native latent action. We further propose a pretraining paradigm for vision-language-action (VLA) policies, Pretraining Actions from World models (PAWlicy), in which Native LAM serves as a dynamics teacher on large-scale video; unlike world action models, it never generates video. Native latent actions outperform existing LAMs on the LARY benchmark in both action classification and control regression, and replay the same motion on new robots, in new scenes, and from human hands to robots, although no transfer objective is used in training. With a 3.8B model, PAWlicy reaches a 93.6% average success rate on RoboTwin 2.0 trained with domain-randomized demonstrations, the highest among VLAs. On RoboDojo, it is competitive on every dimension we evaluate, and its Precision, evaluated by us, is on par with the leading leaderboard entries. On real robots, it improves over the pi_0.5 baseline on both tasks. Both stages use only public data and a publicly released world model.
papers.title_zh: 世界模型即原生潜在动作模型
papers.summary_zh: 直接用视频世界模型充当潜在动作模型，从无动作的人类和机器人视频中恢复共享动作空间。

papers.title: HIVE-Bench: Evaluating Patch-Level Visual Representations for Egocentric Robot Manipulation
papers.abstract: Pretrained vision is a common start for robot learning, but most comparisons still score one pooled vector from a third-person image. Bimanual policies instead read dense patch tokens from cameras on the robot. We introduce HIVE-Bench: one shared flow-matching policy reads 20 encoders from seven families on 24 egocentric bimanual tasks, across adaptation, task sharing, and sweeps of data, model size, and layer. Keeping the patches matters. Averaging each view to one token removes most of the success, adaptation helps every pair we test, and one shared policy keeps most of the success of separate policies at a fraction of the updates. The same tokens are then scored with statistics, state and object readouts, published vision scores, and an inverse-dynamics readout. That readout of the commanded motion is one of the strongest measurements available before a policy is trained. Recognition, depth, and correspondence do not transfer reliably. Fine-tuning can improve the action readout even when other measurements move the other way, and no statistic is stable enough to replace a rollout before any deployment.
papers.title_zh: HIVE-Bench：评测第一人称机器人操作中的 patch 级视觉表征
papers.summary_zh: 在 24 个双臂第一人称任务上，用同一个 flow-matching 策略比较 7 类共 20 个视觉编码器。

papers.title: Self-WSP: Can Language Models Improve Themselves Through Weight-Space Programming?
papers.abstract: Frontier language models can now read and edit the weights of a neural network much like code and thereby improve a small model, an approach known as Weight-Space Programming (WSP). We further explore applying WSP to a language model itself, which we call Self-WSP. Specifically, Qwen3.5-0.8B reads its own weights, proposes an edit, and then continues with the edited weights as both problem solver and editor. We find many cases of genuine self-improvement. Self-edits can raise GSM8K accuracy from 11.8% to 62.2% and MATH500 accuracy from 7.0% to 32.2%, sometimes by changing only 16 parameters, and in some cases repeated self-editing keeps improving the model. A closer look, however, reveals that these gains lack interpretability. The model shows little understanding of the edits it makes, and WSP driven by random search sometimes performs comparably. Self-WSP thus holds promise as a path toward recursive self-improvement (RSI), but realizing this promise requires further exploration.
papers.title_zh: Self-WSP：语言模型能否通过权重空间编程自我改进？
papers.summary_zh: 让 Qwen3.5-0.8B 读取自身权重并提出修改，再继续训练，检验权重空间编程用于自我改进。

papers.title: WeightCode: Installing New Capabilities into Neural Networks via Weight-Space Programming
papers.comment: 26 pages, 11 figures, including appendix. Code: https://github.com/Gen-Verse/WeightCode
papers.abstract: Neural networks encode learned capabilities in their weights, yet extending those capabilities with explicit task knowledge remains a fundamental challenge. Here we show that Weight-Space Programming (WSP), in which executable programs read, construct or modify a network's weights directly, can install new capabilities within trained neural networks. WeightCode, a WSP framework, uses a frozen language model to write executable weight programs that install new computations into trained neural networks using task knowledge and their existing weights, without gradient-based training. Once installed, the new capabilities run independently of the language model. Given a grammar or eight demonstrations, weight programs enable previously unseen command compositions (0% to 99.8% exact match) and a new pickup action (0% to 98.4% success), while preserving the original command and navigation capabilities. On ImageNet, four weight programs achieve net gains of 8.84-17.62 points while preserving clean accuracy, outperforming the best of eight fine-tuning methods under matched examples, checks, and retention constraints. In a Vision Transformer, causal interventions show that installed noise-correction gates drive robustness gains, while their selective activation preserves clean accuracy. Rerun on five independently trained Vision Transformers without further language model calls, ten weight programs retain 83-110% of their source-network gains on average, whereas copying their fixed weight edits yields negligible gains. Six programs written for an already edited network add 5.23-14.50 points of contrast robustness while retaining the previously installed noise gain. Together, these results establish WSP as a new route to acquiring and accumulating capabilities in trained neural networks through reusable weight programs.
papers.title_zh: WeightCode：通过权重空间编程向神经网络植入新能力
papers.summary_zh: 用可执行程序直接读取、构造或修改网络权重，在已训练网络中安装新能力。

papers.title: Innata-0: A Native Embodied World System with Model-Agent Co-Design
papers.abstract: The physical world is open-ended, dynamic, and partially observable. While foundation models have advanced embodied intelligence, standalone models struggle with long-horizon execution, and simply integrating models with agents may lead to inconsistencies between planning and physical control. To support reliable and adaptive behaviors in the physical world, we introduce Innata-0, a native embodied world system. Innata-0 jointly designs an embodied world-action model and an agent to combine their complementary strengths. The model, Innata-0-WAM, adopts a tri-tower Mixture-of-Transformers architecture that integrates understanding, prediction, and action generation. The agent, Innata-0-Agent, coordinates long-horizon execution through memory, verification, and recovery. A co-design protocol is further proposed to align model training with agent execution and leverage validated experiences to support subsequent adaptation and model improvement. Extensive evaluations demonstrate strong embodied capabilities across understanding, world prediction, and robotic manipulation. Innata-0 represents our first step toward physical intelligence, and we see it as the beginning of a much longer journey.
papers.title_zh: Innata-0：模型与智能体协同设计的原生具身世界系统
papers.summary_zh: 面向开放物理世界，将模型与智能体协同设计，以缓解规划与物理控制不一致。

papers.title: AutoPILOT: A Visual Agent Harness for Real-Time Gameplay
papers.comment: 33 pages, 10 figures, 21 tables. Project page: https://autopilot-harness.github.io/
papers.abstract: Multimodal foundation models can play video games well when the game waits for them, but often fail when it keeps running. We find that much of this gap lies in the harness, which decides what the model sees, what it remembers, and how its outputs become actions over time. Existing harnesses such as VISTA improve the first two, yet turn each model call into at most one action, so the agent acts only as often as its model thinks. We introduce AutoPILOT, which changes the third: in each model call, the model can send a primitive action, start an open-loop macro, or write a closed-loop controller that keeps playing from the screen without further model calls until it hands control back. To evaluate agents in real-time games, we build AFK-Bench, 120 diverse browser games grouped by how they respond to inaction and playable in real time or with the clock paused. With GPT-6.1 Sol under the same budgets, AutoPILOT reaches 68.6% real-time success against 38.3% for VISTA, and on GameWorld it keeps 80.0% in real time while VISTA drops from 84.1% to 42.9%. Its gains hold across closed and open-source models, and it reaches VISTA's final success rate at a fifth of its API cost. Our results suggest that how a harness turns model outputs into actions over time is a central yet underexplored part of agent design, and we hope AutoPILOT and AFK-Bench will serve as a foundation for agents in a world that does not wait.
papers.title_zh: AutoPILOT：面向实时游戏的视觉智能体 Harness
papers.summary_zh: 设计让多模态模型在游戏持续运行时仍能决策的 Harness，缩小与等待式游戏之间的差距。

papers.title: MomentMem: Memorizing Key Moments for Robot Manipulation
papers.abstract: Robotic manipulation often requires remembering visual information that is no longer observable, such as the original location of an object. Existing approaches typically rely on full observation histories, which become redundant over long horizons, or text summaries, which may omit precise visual details. We study visual moment memory, the ability to retain such details from key moments for subsequent manipulation. To support this study, we introduce VMBench, a suite of long-horizon manipulation tasks requiring memory of spatial locations, visual appearances, and their associations. We further propose MomentMem, a hierarchical architecture in which a VLM-based memorizer selects keyframes and an executor predicts actions conditioned on the selected memories. This separation enables us to evaluate memory selection alongside closed-loop task success and to study memorizer generalization independently of the executor. On VMBench, MomentMem achieves 49.9% average success, outperforming the strongest evaluated baseline by 31.7 percentage points. Moreover, we find that the memorizer transfers well to unseen appearances zero-shot. It can also adapt to an unseen task with only a few memory annotations, reaching 43.7% success, close to the 44.3% obtained with full memory supervision. Further experiments show competitive performance on RMBench and improvements in real-robot manipulation. These results highlight the value of retaining sparse visual evidence for memory-dependent manipulation. Our code is available at https://github.com/PKU-VaLuE-Lab/MomentMem.
papers.title_zh: MomentMem：为机器人操作记住关键时刻
papers.summary_zh: 研究视觉关键时刻记忆，让操作策略只保留必要的历史画面而非完整观测序列。

papers.title: Fast-JEPA: Advancing the Success-Latency Frontier for Latent World Models
papers.abstract: Latent world models predict the outcomes of action sequences, but comparing candidate plans through recursive rollout remains expensive at test time. We introduce Fast-JEPA, a latent world model planning framework that advances the success-latency Pareto frontier of predictive search. Fast-JEPA reorganizes predictive computation to support effective action-sequence search at low planning cost. It constructs a goal-directed plan to guide search and directly predicts the outcomes of complete candidates for efficient comparison, avoiding recursive state rollout during refinement. Across PushT, Reacher, Cube, and TwoRoom, Fast-JEPA achieves 96.50% average success rate with 2.41x faster planning than INTACT. Search-budget sweeps show that its competitive success and low latency extend across candidate counts and refinement depths. We further introduce DynaGoal, a benchmark for evaluating world-model planning under dynamic out-of-distribution conditions, execution deadlines, and controlled response delays. Fast-JEPA achieves average success rates of 73.83% on DynaGoal-Shift and 87.67% on DynaGoal-Deadline, demonstrating the practical value of low-latency predictive planning under changing control conditions and execution-time constraints. Our project page is available at https://deepcybo-physai.github.io/Fast-JEPA.
papers.title_zh: Fast-JEPA：推进潜在世界模型的成功率-延迟前沿
papers.summary_zh: 重组潜在世界模型的预测计算，降低规划时递归 rollout 的测试开销。

papers.title: Wactorz: Self-Writing LLM Agents That Discover, Repair, and Migrate at the Edge
papers.comment: 5 pages. 2 figues. Extended version of a paper accepted to the AAAI-27 Demonstrations Program. Code: https://github.com/waldiez/wactorz
papers.abstract: Most LLM agent frameworks build a crew that runs a task and exits. Physical environments (e.g., homes, labs, factory floors) need agents that stay up for months, survive their own bugs, and run on whatever hardware is already next to the sensors. We present Wactorz, an open-source runtime in which LLM-generated agents are long-lived, supervised actors: a planner turns a chat request into Python, compiles it into a new actor at runtime, and a supervisor restarts that actor alone, with its state intact, when it crashes. All coordination rides on MQTT, so agents can be spawned on, and live-migrated between, edge nodes such as a Raspberry Pi, and every internal event is a topic external systems can subscribe to. The recorded demo builds a camera-to-lamp automation from one chat request, adds a second agent that is auto-wired to the first by topic and carries a deliberate division-by-zero, watches that agent repair its own code without losing its count, then deploys a fresh Raspberry Pi node and live-migrates the agent onto it, in under four minutes of wall-clock time and \$0.13 of model usage. This extended version adds what the two-page demonstration paper could not: the Wiring view of the topic graph, Wactorz as a library for hand-written agents, how trained models are stored, sent to nodes and replaced, the security model, and the system's limitations.
papers.title_zh: Wactorz：在边缘端自行编写、发现、修复和迁移的 LLM 智能体
papers.summary_zh: 开源运行时，让 LLM 生成的智能体长期驻留、受监督运行，并可在边缘设备间迁移。

papers.title: Embodied-Harness: Towards Recursive Self-Improvement for Robotic Manipulation
papers.abstract: Vision-language model (VLM)-based agents offer a promising approach to robotic manipulation, yet remain limited by inadequate memory organization, uncertain failure attribution, and limited reuse of execution experience. We propose Embodied-Harness, a dual-agent framework that improves manipulation by refining the execution harness without updating model parameters. The Actor interacts with the environment through a robot-control interface, while the Reflector converts execution evidence into reusable operational guidance. Hierarchical Memory Architecture maintains short-term execution context and long-term experiential knowledge to support execution and reflection. Evidence-based Experience Reflection grounds failure diagnosis in observed interactions, while Recursive Harness Self-Improvement refines operational guidance across successive attempts. Experiments on RoboTwin 2.0, RoboSPA, and RMBench demonstrate the effectiveness of Embodied-Harness in generalization under environmental variations, spatial reasoning, long-horizon planning, and memory-dependent manipulation. Our method achieves success rates of 82.4%, 76.7%, and 94.4% on the three benchmarks, respectively. Real-world evaluation further yields an average success rate of 96.7% across three manipulation tasks. These results highlight the potential of Embodied-Harness to improve robotic manipulation through experience-driven harness self-improvement.
papers.title_zh: Embodied-Harness：迈向机器人操作的递归自我改进
papers.summary_zh: 双智能体框架在不更新模型的前提下改进执行 Harness，处理记忆组织、失败归因和经验复用。

papers.title: MMMem: Self-Improving Agents with Task-Aware Multimodal Experience Consolidation
papers.abstract: AI agents accumulate conversations, images, and documents through long-term interactions with users. Answering later questions often requires connecting evidence across these records, yet the resulting understanding is rarely retained, allowing mistakes to recur on related questions. Existing multimodal memory methods largely focus on storing and retrieving records, with limited mechanisms for learning from completed tasks and consolidating task-specific experience. We therefore propose MMMem, a task-aware multimodal memory framework that extracts and consolidates experience from completed tasks through four complementary strategies. First, source-linked multi-view memory organizes original text, images, and rendered pages alongside generated scene images that combine clues across records for retrieval. Second, source-generated tasks support knowledge alignment at two levels: warm-up consolidates source knowledge into task-relevant experiences in external memory, while self-training adapts the model's parametric knowledge to task demands. Third, the same vision-language model distills completed tasks into experiences that record the task context, conclusion, and support links. Finally, task-aware retrieval recalls source views and relevant experiences for answering and verification, while source-supported reuse guides long-term retention. Across three memory benchmarks and two vision-language readers, MMMem outperforms eight baselines. With Qwen3.5-9B, MMMem achieves relative gains of 36.9%, 17.6%, and 15.2% over the best-performing baselines on LoCoMo, Mem-Gallery, and LooGLE v2, respectively. Ablations show consistent gains from training and memory warm-up, while case studies illustrate how individual components work in practice.
papers.title_zh: MMMem：任务感知的多模态经验整合实现智能体自我改进
papers.summary_zh: 把交互中积累的多模态记录整合为任务相关的经验，避免智能体在相关问题上重复犯错。

papers.title: ToolSmith: An Automatic Tool-Generation Framework for Multimodal Search Agents
papers.abstract: Recent multimodal search agents use reasoning, vision, and live web search across many turns to answer questions beyond parametric knowledge by orchestrating a small library of hand-crafted search and visual tools. However, the library is laborious to create and maintain, and frozen when new query types, evidence formats, and failure modes are encountered in the wild. Human practitioners, by contrast, cope with insufficient tools by fashioning new ones from familiar parts and reusing them across tasks. Inspired by this, we propose ToolSmith, an automatic tool-generation framework that grows and reuses modules on top of a lean base tool library. We evaluate ToolSmith on three in-domain multimodal search benchmarks and ten out-of-domain benchmarks under a VLM-as-a-Judge protocol. ToolSmith consistently improves over the base library across deployed agents of varying scales, with larger backbones reaping greater gains, demonstrating the scalability of the approach. Our code and data are available at https://threesr.github.io/toolsmith/.
papers.title_zh: ToolSmith：面向多模态搜索智能体的自动工具生成框架
papers.summary_zh: 自动生成并维护多模态搜索智能体所需的搜索与视觉工具，替代手工维护的固定工具库。

papers.title: Beam Model Technical Report
papers.abstract: Beam is a sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model with 501.3B total parameters and 23.4B active parameters, specifically built and optimized for coding, reasoning, and agentic workloads. Beam delivers frontier level reasoning, while requiring 3-4x less inference compute than many models of its class. Pretrained on 23.8T diverse, curated, high-quality tokens, Beam features a 1M-token context window achieved through a novel two-stage midtraining phase, built on verifiable, correctness-anchored data. Post-training leveraged a large-scale, fully asynchronous reinforcement learning (RL) campaign across 10.5K GB300 GPUs, generating over 100M rollouts over 4 weeks of training. We believe this is one of the largest scale RL runs conducted by any open lab to date. Across our evaluation suite, capabilities continued to improve as we increased RL compute, with no sign of a plateau. Supported by deep hardware-model co-design, FP8/NVFP4 quantization, and a 1.93B-parameter speculative decoding drafter (DFlash 2), Beam maximizes serving throughput with efficient, flexible deployment. Averaged across conversation turns and harm categories, Beam refuses or pivots on 88.9% of harmful requests while complying with 81.5% of harmless requests, achieving the highest refusal/pivot rate on harmful requests among open-weight models on the Pareto frontier.
papers.title_zh: Beam 模型技术报告
papers.summary_zh: 稀疏 MoE 模型 Beam 总参数 501.3B、激活 23.4B，面向代码、推理和 Agent 场景，预训练 23.8T token。

llm.star_why: 501B MoE 技术报告，主打低推理成本

papers.title: PixelOne: From Options to Pixels in a Single Forward for GUI Grounding
papers.abstract: GUI grounding requires precise clicks at low latency. Recent models such as GUI-Decisions and GUI-Swift predict coordinates in one forward pass using fixed global bins with local refinement. However, screenshot downsampling removes detail needed to locate small controls, while fixed bins cover larger pixel ranges at higher resolutions. We introduce PixelOne, which transfers spatial knowledge from a search teacher to a student that predicts clicks directly from screenshots at native resolution. The teacher uses VideoJEV's text-option scorer to select rows and columns and progressively zoom into candidate regions. The student inherits the teacher's parameters and matches its distributions over explored regions through spatial distillation alongside box supervision. At inference, the same decision head selects a visual token, and a lightweight pixel head predicts the click within it, all in one forward pass. A click-aligned loss encourages pixels inside the target box to score above those outside. Across four benchmarks, PixelOne-Pro-35B-A3B achieves 83.8% mean accuracy, the highest among the evaluated single-forward grounders, with a mean latency of 0.43 s per target.
papers.title_zh: PixelOne：单次前向从选项到像素的 GUI 定位
papers.summary_zh: 改进单次前向 GUI 定位的坐标预测，解决截图降采样丢失小控件细节、固定分箱覆盖过粗的问题。

papers.title: ViDecide: Teaching Video Diffusion Models to Reason and Plan Step by Step
papers.abstract: Current leading video generation models can synthesize highly realistic videos, while still frequently violating physical and logical constraints in multi-step reasoning and planning, even after training with large-scale reasoning data or existing diffusion RL methods. We attribute these failures to the conventional video training paradigm, which treats a solution as a fixed-length clip rather than a chain of decisions. We present ViDecide, a decision-centric framework that trains video diffusion models to predict state transitions causally and decide when to stop, with a decision-focused training schedule. We further propose Corrective Fine-tuning (CFT), which corrects failed decisions by mapping their noise to the model's own successful continuations, achieving stable improvement without policy-gradient optimization. Across abstract games, planning tasks, and a new benchmark of multi-step robot planning, ViDecide achieves an average strict success rate of 83.8%, far above 23.3% for standard fine-tuning and 67.8% for the strongest prior method, and generalizes to larger puzzles and unseen layouts. Our framework therefore unlocks greater potential for video generation models as reliable reasoners and planners in the visual world. Project page: https://kevin-thu.github.io/ViDecide.
papers.title_zh: ViDecide：教视频扩散模型逐步推理与规划
papers.summary_zh: 改变传统视频训练范式，让视频扩散模型在多步推理与规划中更少违反物理和逻辑约束。

papers.title: Distilling Visual Agents from Limited Interaction Experience
papers.abstract: How much interaction experience is needed to distill a capable visual agent? We study learning from few tasks and recorded interaction histories. Our framework selects representative trajectories using skill-context coverage and ordered visual-decision similarity. On-policy distillation (OPD) learns through fresh interaction on selected tasks or fresh student responses at fixed histories. Across Navigation, Sokoban, and spatial mapping, even one online training task supports transfer to other tasks. Four fixed trajectories raise a 4B student's success from 49.17% to 82.08% on standard Navigation and from 60.16% to 85.55% on Sokoban, recovering over 90% of the measured gap to a 27B teacher on these panels. On an independent Navigation panel, replay improves success from 45.83% to 76.67%, retaining 91.36% of the same-task online gain without new interaction during optimization. Training repetitions, matched supervised fine-tuning (SFT), and a 9B extension further support the value of compact experience.
papers.title_zh: 从有限交互经验中蒸馏视觉智能体
papers.summary_zh: 研究少量任务和交互记录需要多少经验才能蒸馏出能力足够的视觉智能体，并给出轨迹选择方法。

papers.title: SAVIOR: Sample-efficient Adaptation of Vision-Language Models for OCR Representation
papers.abstract: Optical Character Recognition (OCR) pipelines and vision-language models exhibit high accuracy on standard OCR and document-understanding benchmarks, yet they systematically underperform on document patterns that are operationally critical in financial workflows. These patterns include vertical or rotated text, logo-embedded vendor names, fine-print regulatory clauses, degraded scans, and complex multi-column layouts. While underrepresented in public datasets, they constitute a substantial portion of real-world failure cases. We introduce SAVIOR, a sample-efficient data curation methodology that targets such high-impact failure scenarios to adapt vision-language models for robust financial OCR. We further propose PaIRS, a structure-aware evaluation metric that measures layout fidelity by comparing pairwise spatial relationships between tokens. Fine-tuning Qwen2.5-VL-Instruct with SAVIOR-Train achieves a word recall of 0.93. When the resulting layout-aware OCR output is used as context for document question answering, it attains an F1 score of 0.89, outperforming both open- and closed-source models such as GPT-4o, Mistral-OCR, PaddleOCR-VL, and DeepSeek-OCR.
papers.title_zh: SAVIOR：面向 OCR 表征的视觉语言模型样本高效适配
papers.summary_zh: 针对金融场景中竖排、旋转文字、含 logo 的供应商名称等难点，样本高效地适配 VLM 的 OCR 能力。

papers.title: LLMs Memorize Their Own Hallucinations During Post-Training
papers.abstract: Reasoning domains have shaped the post-training recipes of frontier models even though they are trained and deployed in domains beyond math and code. In this paper, we study the consequences of directly adopting reasoning-centric training recipes, e.g., the use of outcome-based rewards for reinforcement learning (RL), injection of "cognitive" behaviors such as proposing and backtracking from hypotheses in reasoning chains, etc., for knowledge tasks. We hypothesize that these decisions, while useful for reasoning, inadvertently encourage models to memorize hallucinations they themselves generate in their long reasoning chains when trained on knowledge tasks. To study this, we train models with standard post-training, extract their self-generated hallucinations during RL, and track memorization throughout the rest of training. Our experiments on six open models across two model families and two architectures confirm our hypothesis. We find that models' recall of hallucinations reinforced during training increases by 4.83% on average, compared to just 0.17% for self-hallucinations that receive no training signal. In fact, models even memorize false facts that they immediately retract in their reasoning; a backtracking template inherited from reasoning-centric training that has no benefit for knowledge recall. Furthermore, we find that memorization is strongest on the hardest training questions, and rewarding a hallucination makes the model less likely to abstain from it later (by 7.23% on average). Overall, our work identifies and systematically studies a previously unexamined pathway through which models learn hallucinations during training.
papers.title_zh: LLM 在后训练中记住了自己的幻觉
papers.summary_zh: 研究把以推理为中心的后训练配方（结果奖励 RL、认知行为注入等）直接用于其他领域带来的后果。

papers.title: Single-Transformer Latent Diffusion
